Incorporating July 2020 SLOOS insights into the assessment of the September 16, 2020 FOMC statement:

- The FOMC’s highly accommodative stance and improved market functioning are positive, but SLOOS shows a broad-based tightening of bank lending standards and terms for C&I loans (across firm sizes), commercial real estate, and most consumer credit categories. Banks also reported weaker demand for C&I and CRE loans and expected further tightening due to elevated uncertainty, lower risk tolerance, and concerns about collateral values.
- While low rates boosted mortgage demand, banks tightened mortgage standards as well; HELOCs and other consumer credit saw tighter standards and softer demand. This suggests bank credit supply is constrained precisely where policy transmission to Main Street matters most, especially for SMEs and CRE.
- Net effect: SLOOS corroborates and amplifies the FOMC’s cautious outlook by indicating tighter bank intermediation and potential headwinds to credit growth, partially offsetting the support from asset purchases and facilities.

Given these SLOOS findings, the balance shifts more negative than the FSR-based read.
